tools.description:
Edit or restyle images with a text prompt. Cost: nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9, GPT Image models 12 credits.
Give exactly ONE reference source: input_task_id (all images of an earlier image task), reference_file_paths (local files; never base64-encode them yourself) or reference_image_urls.

remove_background.description: Transparent-background PNG (no effect on multi-view output).

Turn a textured model into a multi-color 3MF that opens ready to print in the slicer of printer_brand. Cost: 10 credits.

tools.name: get_item_doc
tools.description: Get documentation for a Mantine component, hook, guide or FAQ page. Without a section it returns an outline (description plus section list) — pass a section to fetch just that part, or full:true for the whole page.

section.description: Section slug from the outline, e.g. "zod"

full.description: Return the entire page; can be very large

tools.name: get_item_props
tools.description: Get props for a Mantine component, or the TypeScript signature for a hook. Pages documenting an API in prose point at the relevant section instead.

tools.name: list_items
tools.description: List Mantine documentation items, filtered by kind, nav group, category, package or a text query.

tools.name: get_api
tools.description: Resolve a Mantine symbol (useForm, useDisclosure, UseFormReturnType) to its TypeScript signature and exported types, without knowing which page documents it.

error: the package has 0 bins (none); set subject.bin

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Call this tool FIRST to retrieve the fully structured documentation header as JSON. Returns hierarchical sections with parsed content (no raw markdown). Includes installation instructions, critical notices, and subsections with their content and code blocks. This provides essential context before exploring specific components.

tools.name: get_list_components
tools.description: List all Taiga UI documentation section IDs (structured JSON only).

tools.name: get_component_example
tools.description: Return section-related content snippets (formerly examples) for specified documentation section name(s). The presence of id indicates a successful match.

tools.name: get_migration_guide
tools.description: Returns the complete Migration Guide for Taiga UI updates. Includes step-by-step migration instructions, troubleshooting, and common issues. Call this tool when you need to migrate between Taiga UI versions.

tools.name: get-current-time
tools.description: Get the current time in the configured local timezone

tools.name: get-current-timezone
tools.description: Get the current system timezone

tools.name: get-time-in-timezone
tools.description: Get the current time in a specific timezone

timezone.description: The timezone to get the current time for

tools.name: list-timezones
tools.description: List all available timezones

tools.name: cache_get
tools.description: Get a value from a running cache instance by key. Returns the stored value (string or deserialized JSON object) or null if the key does not exist or has expired. Read-only — no side effects. Use cache_mget when you need multiple keys in one round-trip. Use cache_exists to check existence without retrieving the value. Use semantic_search when you need fuzzy/vector search across stored values.

key.description: Cache key to retrieve

org_id.description: Optional org ID — if the direct key misses, falls back to the shared org namespace org:{org_id}:sem:{key}

tools.name: cache_set
tools.description: Set a key-value pair in a running cache instance. Overwrites any existing value at the key — not idempotent for new data. Returns "OK" on success; returns an error if the instance_id is invalid or the instance is paused. Value can be a string or a JSON-serialized object. Optionally set a TTL in seconds (omit for no expiry). Use cache_mset instead for setting multiple keys in a single pipeline round-trip. Use cache_stream_set instead for caching LLM token streams (ordered string chunks).

instance_id.description: UUID of the cache instance (from list_instances)

key.description: Cache key

value.description: Value to store (string or JSON)

ttl.description: Time-to-live in seconds (optional, omit for no expiry)

org_id.description: Optional org ID — also writes the key to the shared org namespace org:{org_id}:sem:{key} with the same TTL

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Find cached entries that are semantically similar to a natural-language query. Read-only — no side effects. Returns an array of objects, each with: key, value, similarity_score (0–1), and namespace. Returns an empty array if no entries meet the similarity threshold. Requires OPENAI_API_KEY (or compatible provider) and CACHLY_VECTOR_URL; every tier includes a vector token. Embeddings are computed server-side and never leave Germany (pgvector HNSW index). Example: "find all cached responses about password reset" or "what did we answer about pricing?". Use cache_get for exact key lookup; use smar

instance_id.description: UUID of the cache instance (from list_instances)

query.description: Natural-language query to find similar cached content

threshold.description: Minimum cosine similarity 0–1 (default: 0.82). Lower = broader matches.

namespace.description: Semantic namespace to search in (default: cachly:sem)

top_k.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

use_hybrid.description: Enable Hybrid BM25+Vector RRF fusion search. Passes `hybrid: true` and the query text to the pgvector API for higher precision on named entities. Default: false.

auto_namespace.description: Auto-detect the namespace from the query text using text heuristics instead of using the `namespace` parameter. Returns results only from the matching domain (code/translation/summary/qa/creative).

tools.name: index_project
tools.description: Index local source files into the cachly semantic cache so AI assistants can use semantic_search to find relevant files instead of re-reading the whole codebase every time. Walks a directory recursively, reads each matching file, and stores a summary + path as a semantic cache entry (prompt = file path + content excerpt, value = relative path). Requires an embedding provider (OPENAI_API_KEY or CACHLY_EMBED_PROVIDER + key). Run once, then re-run after major refactors. TTL=86400 (24h) keeps entries fresh.

dir.description: Absolute path to the directory to index (e.g. /Users/you/myproject/src)

max_files.description: Maximum number of files to index (default: 100)

ttl.description: TTL in seconds for indexed entries (default: 86400 = 24 h)

summary_chars.description: Characters to use as summary per file (default: 1200)

namespace.description: Semantic namespace to store under (default: cachly:sem:code)

tools.name: remember_context
tools.description: Save context information to the cache so you can recall it later without re-computing. Perfect for caching: codebase overviews, file summaries, project structure, frequently-accessed data, or "thinking" results like dependency analysis. The AI assistant can use this to avoid re-reading the entire codebase every time. Overwrites any existing value stored under the same key. Returns { key, stored_at, ttl } confirming the saved context. Example: remember_context("project overview", "This is a Next.js app with...") then later: recall_context("project overview"). Use recall_context to retrieve; use

key.description: Descriptive key like "project_overview", "auth_architecture", "file:src/index.ts"

category.description: Category for organization (default: custom)

ttl.description: Time-to-live in seconds (default: 86400 = 24h, use 0 for no expiry)

tools.name: recall_context
tools.description: Retrieve previously saved context from the cache. Returns the saved content or null if not found. Use this at the START of any task to check if you already have relevant context cached, before doing expensive operations like reading many files. Supports glob patterns: "file:*" matches all file summaries, "arch*" matches architecture-related keys.

key.description: The key to look up (supports glob pattern like "file:*")

tools.name: list_remembered
tools.description: List all cached context entries for this project. Shows what knowledge the AI assistant has already cached, so you can decide whether to recall existing context or refresh it. Returns: key, category, size, TTL remaining, and a content preview.

category.description: Filter by category (default: all)

tools.name: forget_context
tools.description: Delete one or more cached context entries. Use when context is stale or you want to force a fresh analysis. Supports glob patterns: "file:*" deletes all file summaries.

tools.name: learn_from_attempts
tools.description: Store a lesson AFTER any non-trivial task (deploy, debug, fix, decision); future sessions recall it. instance_id may be omitted; the configured instance is used — never guess one. If the topic already exists, the write is an UPDATE and REQUIRES `grund` (one line: WHY the previous version was wrong) — without it the update is rejected. A conflicting outcome triggers a contradiction warning. Example: learn_from_attempts(topic="deploy:api", outcome="success", what_worked="PORT 3095 SERVES WHISPER — nohup docker compose up -d", severity="critical")

what_worked.description: What solved it. LEAD WITH THE DECISIVE FACT (the number, address, command) in the first 100 characters — briefings truncate there.

what_failed.description: What did NOT work (optional but valuable)

context.description: The SYMPTOM in the words someone would search for, before they knew the fix ("deploy stuck, rollout not finishing"). Plus error messages and root cause. Optional but high-value: it is what closes the gap between the question and the answer.

severity.description: Impact severity: critical (blocks work/deploy), major (significant slowdown), minor (nice to know). Default: major.

commands.description: Commands that worked or failed (e.g. ["rsync -avz ...", "docker compose up -d"])

depends_on.description: Prerequisites, e.g. ["node:>=20", "docker:running"]. A stale one flags dependent lessons for review.

author.description: Who is storing this lesson, e.g. "alice". Enables cross-author reuse tracking.

grund.description: One line: WHY the previous version was wrong, like a commit message. REQUIRED when the topic already exists; optional on first write.

ersetzt.description: Topic slug of an OLDER lesson this one refutes. The old one is suppressed in smart_recall and shows a "superseded" banner.

gilt_ab.description: ISO date since when the FACT is true (vs. when written). Omit if unknown. A replacement sets gilt_bis on the old lesson (then shown as history). About the fact, NOT an age decay.

gilt_fuer.description: Version scope of the FACT, package@range, all must hold: ["next@<15", "react@>=18 <19", "go@>=1.22", "python:fastapi@<0.110"]. Recall ranks a lesson that does not fit the project versions last, marked, never hidden; unknown = no change. Omit on update to keep, [] clears.

visibility.description: Who can see it: "team" (default) = all members, "private" = only via exact recall_best_solution, "public" = same as team for now.

service.description: Service or system this lesson concerns, e.g. "prometheus", "auth-service".

service_kind.description: "service" (default) for an application, "system" for infrastructure like prometheus or redis.

group.description: Optional sub-team scope, e.g. "backend". Only that group and admins see it. Independent of visibility.

tools.name: recall_best_solution
tools.description: Recall the best known solution for a topic from past lessons. Call this BEFORE attempting any task that might have been done before. Returns the most recent successful lesson for the topic, with confidence indicator. ⚠️ badge = lesson is >5d old (verify before applying). 🔴 = >10d old (likely stale!). Recalling a lesson resets its confidence clock to 1.0 (marks as recently verified). A superseded lesson shows a banner naming its successor; if the successor was deleted, the banner says so and the lesson counts as the best remaining answer. Example: recall_best_solution(topic="deploy:web") → ret

topic.description: Topic slug to look up, e.g. "deploy:web". Supports partial match.

author.description: Who is asking (optional). Required to read a group-scoped lesson: without it, group-scoped lessons answer like "not found". Team-wide lessons need no author.

tools.name: smart_recall
tools.description: Returns the fixes, decisions and pitfalls this team already learned for the task at hand. Call it FIRST at the start of every coding task — before reading files or editing — with one line about the task, e.g. smart_recall("fix login redirect loop"). Finds lessons by meaning, not exact words. instance_id may be omitted; the configured instance is used — never guess one. Falls back to remember_context keys if no semantic match is found.

query.description: Natural language query to find relevant cached context

author.description: Who is recalling (optional). Counts cross-author reuse.

context_files.description: Files you are working on, e.g. ["src/auth/service.ts"]. Lessons learned around these files rank higher.

tools.name: session_start
tools.description: Single-call session briefing for the START of a session: last summary, recent lessons, health. It does not replace smart_recall for a concrete task. Returns: last session summary, recent lessons sorted by recency, relevant lessons for your focus area, brain health stats (counts of open failures and stale lessons), team telepathy (what teammates learned this week), predictive pre-warnings (if your focus area has known failure patterns), and memory crystals (compressed wisdom from old sessions). Also saves a session start marker so session_end can compute duration.

focus.description: Keywords for what you plan to work on today (e.g. "deploy infra api"). Used to surface relevant lessons at the top.

author.description: Your name or handle (e.g. "alice"). Enables Team Telepathy — filters YOUR lessons vs TEAM lessons from past 7 days.

provider.description: Current AI provider (e.g. "claude-code", "copilot", "cursor", "windsurf"). Shown in the briefing header and saved so the next provider can see who was last active.

workspace_path.description: Absolute path to the project root. If no session_end was found (e.g. context limit hit), reads git log to reconstruct what happened since last session.

tools.name: session_end
tools.description: Save a session summary when you finish working. Records what was accomplished, files changed, and lesson count. The next session_start will show this summary as "Last session". Call this when ending a work session, before going idle, or before summarizing. Ambient Learning: if workspace_path is provided, reads git log since session start and auto-learns from commits.

summary.description: Brief summary of what was accomplished this session (2-3 sentences)

lessons_learned.description: Number of new lessons stored this session (optional)

workspace_path.description: Absolute path to the project root (e.g. "/Users/you/myproject"). Enables Ambient Learning — reads git log since session start and auto-learns from commit messages.

tools.name: session_handoff
tools.description: Save a detailed handoff for the NEXT chat window / session. Stores: current progress, TODO list (done + remaining), changed files with descriptions, instructions for the next assistant, and any incomplete work. The next session_start automatically includes this handoff so the new window knows EXACTLY what happened and what remains. Call this BEFORE closing a chat window, especially if work is incomplete. This prevents the "continue" problem where new windows lose context, skip tasks, or produce broken code.

completed_tasks.description: Tasks that were fully completed (e.g. "Implemented brainSearch() in JS SDK")

remaining_tasks.description: Tasks NOT yet done — the next window MUST pick these up

path.description: File path relative to project root

description.description: What was changed and what still needs work

files_changed.description: Changed files with their current state — marks partial/broken files so next window knows to fix them

instructions.description: Free-form instructions for the next assistant. Be specific: what to do next, what to avoid, what broke.

context_summary.description: Brief summary of what happened this session (architecture decisions, key findings, blockers)

blocked_on.description: If work is blocked, describe what is needed to unblock (e.g. "waiting for API deploy", "needs user input on design")

tools.name: team_learn
tools.description: Store a lesson in a shared team brain so all team members benefit. Like learn_from_attempts, but REQUIRES an author name for attribution. Shows up in team_recall with "by <author>" so the team knows who learned it.

instance_id.description: UUID of the shared team brain instance

author.description: Your name or handle (required for team attribution)

tools.name: team_recall
tools.description: Recall lessons from a shared team brain, showing who learned what. Works on any shared instance (all team members using the same instance_id). Shows author, recency, and severity for each lesson. Use this to onboard new team members or find who knows about a topic.

instance_id.description: UUID of the shared team brain instance

topic.description: Topic or keyword to filter lessons (optional)

tools.name: roadmap_add
tools.description: Add a new item to the persistent project roadmap stored in the Brain. Items survive across sessions and editors — the roadmap is always up to date. Use for features, bugs, refactors, or any planned work. Call roadmap_list to see all open items, roadmap_next to get the next actionable item.

title.description: Short title of the task/feature (3–10 words)

description.description: What needs to be done, acceptance criteria, context

tools.name: roadmap_update
tools.description: Update the status, priority, or details of a roadmap item. Use to move items through the lifecycle: planned → in-progress → done (or blocked/cancelled). Also use to add notes/findings while working on an item.

id.description: Item ID returned by roadmap_add or roadmap_list

notes.description: Progress notes, findings, or blockers (appended to existing notes)

tools.name: roadmap_list
tools.description: List all roadmap items, optionally filtered by status, priority, tag, or milestone. Returns items sorted by priority then creation date. Called automatically by session_start to show open work.

status.description: Filter by status. Use 'open' to see planned+in-progress+blocked (default: open)

tools.name: roadmap_next
tools.description: Get the single most important next actionable roadmap item. Returns the highest-priority in-progress item first, then planned items, sorted by priority. Call at session start to immediately know what to work on next.

tools.name: brain_doctor
tools.description: Check the health of your AI Brain and get actionable recommendations. Reports: lesson count, context entries, last session age, open failures, quality score, effective IQ boost, stale index. Returns a prioritized list of issues with fix instructions.

workspace_path.description: Absolute path to workspace root — enables package.json analysis for openclaw cross-promo (optional)

tools.name: causal_trace
tools.description: Root Cause Analysis through memory: given a problem description, traces the causal chain from root cause through intermediate failures to the current symptom, then surfaces the exact solution that worked before. Read-only — does not modify any stored data. Requires prior learning: brain must have lessons stored via learn_from_attempts or brain_from_git. Returns an ordered chain of concepts with confidence scores plus the matching solution; returns an empty chain with a message if no causal path is found. Example: causal_trace(problem="auth breaks after restart") → "Root: k8s:namespace-terminat

problem.description: Describe the problem or error you are seeing right now

max_depth.description: Max causal chain depth to trace (default: 5)

tags.description: Optional: narrow search to these tags

tools.name: autopilot
tools.description: Generate a CLAUDE.md / copilot-instructions.md that makes any AI self-managing forever. Writes a configuration file to disk — will overwrite an existing file at the target path. No auth required beyond a valid instance_id. The generated file instructs Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or Gemini to automatically call session_start at window open, learn_from_attempts after every fix, and session_end before closing — without being asked. Returns the generated file content as a string and the path where it was written. Use style="minimal" for just the three hooks; style="full" for the complete ru

project_name.description: Your project name (used in generated instructions)

style.description: minimal = just the hooks, full = full ruleset with examples (default: full)

tools.name: brain_search
tools.description: BM25+ full-text search over ALL brain data: lessons, context entries, session history, CKG nodes, roadmap items. Unlike smart_recall (which focuses on lessons + context), brain_search casts a wider net. Use when smart_recall returns nothing or when you want to find anything the brain knows about a topic.

query.description: What to search for

tools.name: brain_predict
tools.description: READ-ONLY — no side effects, no writes, no external network calls. Predictive Pre-fetch Engine (PPE): given your current context, reads the CKG in your Redis instance to predict likely failures and return the highest-confidence fixes. "Pre-load" means results are returned inline — nothing is cached or persisted. Requires a valid instance_id (your Redis brain). No rate limits. Call at session start when working on a specific feature or debugging area. Set scope="org" to widen prediction across your whole organisation — surfaces cross-team risks ("failed 3× across 2 other teams") from the Org Kn

context.description: What you're working on, e.g. "upgrading Keycloak from 21 to 24"

scope.description: Scope: "instance" (default) = this brain, "org" = warnings from failures in other teams of your organisation, "org+commons" = plus public lessons. Falls back to "instance" without an org.

tools.name: brain_from_git
tools.description: Bootstrap brain lessons from git history. Parses commit messages and infers fix/feature/refactor lessons automatically. Great for onboarding an existing codebase — run once and the brain instantly knows your team's accumulated patterns. Incremental by default: only processes new commits since the last run, so repeated calls are fast. Emits progress updates to stderr during long scans.

repo_path.description: Path to git repository (default: current directory)

branch.description: Git branch to parse (default: current branch / HEAD)

since.description: Only commits after this date, e.g. "2024-01-01" (optional)

incremental.description: Only process commits since last run (default: true). Set false to reprocess all.

tools.name: cachly_tool
tools.description:
Run any of cachly's specialist tools by name.

The most-used tools are listed separately above. This one reaches the
other 98 without their schemas taking up room in every request.

When: compact_recover (after a context limit); brain_predict_failures (before a risky step, with odds); brain_plan (plan a task from past lessons); brain_conflicts (lessons contradict); memory_crystalize (condense lessons).

Unsure about a tool's arguments? Call it with describe:true first — that
returns its input schema instead of running it.

Available: list_instances, create_instance, get_instance, get_connectio

tool.description: Name of the tool to run, e.g. "team_roster".

arguments.description: Arguments for that tool. Use describe:true if unsure.

describe.description: Return the tool's input schema instead of running it.

tools.name: client.chain
tools.description: Execute procedures sequentially

steps.description: The steps, in order: calls or values. A step can read an earlier result as { $ref: name } or { $ref: "$last" }.

passThrough.description: Give each step that has no input the result of the step before

initialInput.description: The input of the first step when passThrough is true

tools.name: client.trace
tools.description: Run the steps of a chain one at a time, and give one row for each step. A step that can write does not run.

steps.description: The steps of a client.chain program, in order: calls or values

passThrough.description: Give each step that has no input the result of the step before

initialInput.description: The input of the first step when passThrough is true

upTo.description: The index of the last step to run (default: all steps)

sampleLimit.description: The most items of each array in the output of a row. The next step gets the full value.

tools.name: client.parallel
tools.description: Execute procedures in parallel

tasks.description: The tasks to run at the same time: calls or values

concurrency.description: The most tasks that run at the same time (default: all)

failFast.description: Stop at the first error (default: false)

tools.name: client.conditional
tools.description: Conditional execution (if/then/else)

condition.description: The condition: a value or a call. A truthy result runs then, a falsy one runs else.

then.description: The program for a truthy condition

else.description: The program for a falsy condition (default: undefined)

tools.name: client.and
tools.description: Short-circuit AND (returns first falsy or last value)

values.description: The operands, in order: values or calls. The evaluation stops at the deciding value.

tools.name: client.or
tools.description: Short-circuit OR (returns first truthy or last value)

values.description: The operands, in order: values or calls. The evaluation stops at the deciding value.

tools.name: client.not
tools.description: Logical NOT of a value

value.description: The value to negate. This procedure does not run a call: a call is an object, thus truthy.

tools.name: client.all
tools.description: Returns true if all values are truthy

values.description: The values to evaluate. This procedure does not run calls: a call is an object, thus truthy. client.and and client.or run calls.

tools.name: client.any
tools.description: Returns true if any value is truthy

values.description: The values to evaluate. This procedure does not run calls: a call is an object, thus truthy. client.and and client.or run calls.

tools.name: client.none
tools.description: Returns true if all values are falsy

values.description: The values to evaluate. This procedure does not run calls: a call is an object, thus truthy. client.and and client.or run calls.

tools.name: client.map
tools.description: Map over an array: run fn for each item (the item is { $ref: "item" })

items.description: The array, or a call that gives it

fn.description: The call to run for each item. It reads the item as { $ref: "item" } (or the name in as) and the position as { $ref: "index" }.

as.description: The $ref name of the item in fn (default: item)

results.description: Results that were computed before (old form)

tools.name: client.reduce
tools.description: Reduce an array: run fn for each item (acc and item are $refs)

items.description: The array, or a call that gives it

fn.description: The call to run for each item. It reads { $ref: "acc" }, { $ref: "item" } and { $ref: "index" }; its result is the next accumulator.

accumulated.description: A result that was computed before (old form)

tools.name: client.identity
tools.description: Return input unchanged

value.description: The value

tools.name: client.constant
tools.description: Return a constant value

value.description: The value

tools.name: client.throw
tools.description: Throw an error

tools.name: client.tryCatch
tools.description: Try/catch wrapper for procedures

catch.description: The program or value for an error. It reads the message as { $ref: "error" }.

tools.name: procedure.define
tools.description: Define a new procedure from an aggregation

path.description: The path of the new procedure, for example ["tools", "double"]

$proc.description: The path of the procedure that the body calls

input.description: The input of that call. It reads the input of the new procedure as { $ref: "input.<field>" }.

$name.description: A name that a $ref can read

aggregation.description: The body of the procedure: a call ({ $proc, input }) that runs, as client.exec runs it, each time the procedure is called

metadata.description: The metadata of the procedure, for example { description, tags }

replace.description: Replace a procedure that procedure.define made at the same path (never a procedure of code)

tools.name: procedure.get
tools.description: Describe a procedure by path or key

path.description: The path, as an array or a dotted key

tools.name: procedure.list
tools.description: List the registered procedures

namespace.description: Only the procedures under this first path segment

includeMetadata.description: Give the whole metadata of each procedure

runtime.description: Only the procedures that procedure.define made

tools.name: procedure.manifest
tools.description: The manifest of the registry: each exposed procedure with its schemas and effects

namespace.description: Only the procedures under this first path segment

tools.name: procedure.delete
tools.description: Delete a runtime-defined procedure

path.description: The path of the procedure to delete (only a procedure that procedure.define made)

tools.name: lib.scan
tools.description: Scan for packages in the git directory

rootPath.description: Workspace root (defaults to the pnpm workspace that contains client-lib)

tools.name: lib.rename
tools.description: Rename a package across the ecosystem

oldName.description: Current package name to rename from

newName.description: New package name to rename to

rootPath.description: Workspace root (defaults to the pnpm workspace that contains client-lib)

tools.name: lib.new
tools.description: Create a new package in the ecosystem

rootPath.description: Workspace root (defaults to the pnpm workspace that contains client-lib)

tools.name: lib.audit
tools.description: Audit ecosystem packages for issues

rootPath.description: Workspace root (defaults to the pnpm workspace that contains client-lib)

fix.description: Attempt to fix issues (create missing files/dirs)

tools.name: lib.graph
tools.description: The dependency graph of the workspace packages: nodes, workspace: edges, cycles and build levels

rootPath.description: The workspace root (default: the pnpm workspace that contains client-lib)

tools.name: lib.importCycles
tools.description: The import cycles of a tree of TypeScript sources: the cycles at runtime (after the import elision), of the declared imports, or of each import

path.description: The folder of the sources, for example packages/web/src

mode.description: The edges to count: runtime (after the import elision, the default), declared or raw

diDecorators.description: The decorators whose class keeps the types of its constructor parameters at runtime (Angular: Injectable, Component, Directive, Pipe, NgModule)

exclude.description: The glob patterns of the files to leave out (default: node_modules, declarations and tests)

limits.description: Lower limits than the defaults. A higher value is refused.

maxFiles.description: The most files of the call: 20000 at most, and the default. A call with more files is refused before it reads a file.

maxFileBytes.description: The largest file that the call reads, in bytes: 1 MiB at most, and the default. The result lists each larger file.

tools.name: procedure.new
tools.description: Scaffold a new procedure with types and registration boilerplate

namespace.description: Namespace override (defaults to first segment of name): the folder under src/procedures

path.description: Project path (defaults to cwd)

tools.name: procedure.export
tools.description: Export a procedure definition as JSON

path.description: Procedure path (array or dot-separated)

tools.name: program.check
tools.description: Check a program before it runs: names, procedures, inputs, the capability and the effects

program.description: The program: a call ({ $proc, input }). The procedure reads it as data: nothing in it starts.

effects.description: The effects that the calls can have. Absent: all effects.

reads.description: The resources that a call can read: names, or "any"

writes.description: The resources that a call can change: names, or "any". An empty list: no change.

grep.description: Filter commits by message pattern (regex supported).

branch.description: Show commits from a specific branch or ref (defaults to current branch).

filePath.description: Show commits that affected a specific file path. Must not start with "-".

oneline.description: Abbreviated output: return only hash, shortHash, and subject per commit. Significantly reduces response size.

stat.description: Include file change statistics for each commit.

patch.description: Include the full diff patch for each commit.

showSignature.description: Show GPG signature verification information for each commit.

tools.name: git_merge
tools.description: Merge branches together. Integrates changes from another branch into the current branch with optional merge strategies.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

branch.description: Branch to merge into current branch.

strategy.description: Merge strategy to use (ort, recursive, octopus, ours, subtree).

squash.description: Squash all commits from the branch into a single commit.

abort.description: Abort an in-progress merge that has conflicts.

tools.name: git_pull
tools.description: Pull changes from a remote repository. Fetches and integrates changes into the current branch.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

rebase.description: Use rebase instead of merge when integrating changes.

fastForwardOnly.description: Fail if can't fast-forward (no merge commit).

tools.name: git_push
tools.description: Push changes to a remote repository. Uploads local commits to the remote branch.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

force.description: Force push (overwrites remote history).

forceWithLease.description: Safer force push - only succeeds if remote branch is at expected state.

setUpstream.description: Set upstream tracking relationship for the branch.

tags.description: Push all tags to the remote.

dryRun.description: Preview the operation without executing it.

remoteBranch.description: Remote branch name to push to (if different from local branch name).

confirmed.description: Explicit confirmation required for force push or branch deletion on protected branches (main, master, production, etc.).

tools.name: git_rebase
tools.description: Rebase commits onto another branch. Reapplies commits on top of another base tip for a cleaner history.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: Rebase operation mode: 'start', 'continue', 'abort', or 'skip'.

upstream.description: Upstream branch to rebase onto (required for start mode).

interactive.description: Interactive rebase (not supported in all providers).

onto.description: Rebase onto different commit than upstream.

tools.name: git_reflog
tools.description: View the reference logs (reflog) to track when branch tips and other references were updated. Useful for recovering lost commits.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

ref.description: Reference whose reflog to show. Defaults to HEAD. Must not start with "-".

maxCount.description: Maximum number of items to return (1-1000).

tools.name: git_remote
tools.description: Manage remote repositories: list remotes, add new remotes, remove remotes, rename remotes, or get/set remote URLs.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: The remote operation to perform.

url.description: Remote URL for add/set-url operations. Accepts HTTP(S), SSH (ssh://… or user@host:path), git://, or file:// URLs. Must not start with "-".

newName.description: New remote name for rename operation.

push.description: Set push URL separately (for set-url operation).

tools.name: git_reset
tools.description: Reset current HEAD to specified state. Can be used to unstage files (soft), discard commits (mixed), or discard all changes (hard).

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: Reset mode: soft (keep changes staged), mixed (unstage changes), hard (discard all changes), merge (reset and merge), keep (reset but keep local changes).

target.description: Target commit to reset to. Defaults to HEAD.

paths.description: Specific file paths to reset (leaves HEAD unchanged). Entries must not start with "-".

confirmed.description: Explicit confirmation required for hard, merge, and keep reset modes on protected branches (main, master, production, etc.).

tools.name: git_set_working_dir
tools.description: Set the session working directory for all git operations so subsequent calls can omit the path parameter. Always returns a repository snapshot (status, recent commits, recent tags, remotes) to orient the caller.

path.description: Absolute path to the git repository to use as the working directory.

validateGitRepo.description: Validate that the path is a Git repository.

initializeIfNotPresent.description: If not a Git repository, initialize it with 'git init'.

tools.name: git_show
tools.description: Show details of a git object (commit, tree, blob, or tag). Displays commit information and the diff of changes introduced.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

object.description: Git object to show (commit hash, branch, tag, tree, or blob).

format.description: Output format for the git object. Use "raw" for unprocessed git output.

stat.description: Show diffstat instead of full diff.

filePath.description: View specific file at a given commit reference. When provided, shows the file content from the specified object. Must not start with "-".

tools.name: git_stash
tools.description: Manage stashes: list stashes, save current changes (push), restore changes (pop/apply), or remove stashes (drop/clear).

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: The stash operation to perform. Defaults to push (save current changes).

stashRef.description: Stash reference like stash@{0} (for pop/apply/drop operations). Must not start with "-".

includeUntracked.description: Include untracked files in the stash (for push operation).

keepIndex.description: Don't revert staged changes (for push operation).

limit.description: For list mode: cap the number of stash entries returned (applied at the git command).

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Show the working tree status including staged, unstaged, and untracked files.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

includeUntracked.description: Include untracked files in the output.

tools.name: git_tag
tools.description: Manage tags: list all tags, create a new tag, delete a tag, or verify a signed tag. Tags are used to mark specific points in history (releases, milestones). Verify runs `git tag -v` and returns a structured result distinguishing unsigned tags, missing trust configuration, bad signatures, and valid signatures.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: The tag operation to perform.

commit.description: Commit to tag (default: HEAD for create operation).

message.description: Tag message. Providing a message always produces an annotated tag (git does not support messages on lightweight tags). For release tags, summarize notable changes.

annotated.description: Create an annotated tag with a default "Tag <name>" message. Only effective when no message is provided and signing is disabled — otherwise the tag is always annotated.

force.description: Overwrite an existing tag (create mode only; has no effect on list or delete).

limit.description: For list mode: cap the number of tags returned (applied at the git command via `--count=N`). Use on repos with many tags.

tools.name: git_worktree
tools.description: Manage multiple working trees: list worktrees, add new worktrees for parallel work, remove worktrees, or move worktrees to new locations.

path.description: Path to the Git repository. Defaults to session working directory set via git_set_working_dir.

mode.description: The worktree operation to perform.

worktreePath.description: Path for the new worktree (for add/move operations). Must not start with "-".

branch.description: For add operation: create a NEW branch with this name in the new worktree. Fails if the branch already exists — use `commitish` to check out an existing branch instead.

commitish.description: For add operation: check out this existing branch/commit/tag in the new worktree (no new branch is created).

force.description: Force operation (for remove operation with uncommitted changes).

newPath.description: New path for the worktree (for move operation). Must not start with "-".

detach.description: Create worktree with detached HEAD (for add operation).

verbose.description: Provide detailed output for worktree operations.

dryRun.description: Preview the operation without executing it (for prune operation).

tools.name: git_wrapup_instructions
tools.description: Returns a Git wrap-up protocol: an acceptance-criteria checklist the agent must satisfy before the session is considered shipped. Uses the operator's custom instructions if configured, otherwise emits a generic goals-strict/mechanism-generic default. Enriches the response with a repository snapshot (status, recent commits, recent tags) so the agent has immediate orientation for the commit and release steps.

acknowledgement.description: Acknowledgement to initiate the wrap-up workflow.

createTag.description: Controls whether the tag criterion appears in the emitted protocol. Omit or set `true` to include the tag step. Set `false` to omit it entirely — e.g., when tagging is deferred to a separate release step.
